title: Lantern-lined causeway across an abyss to a guarded door
what: From a cave mouth framed by two carved totem pillars a straight cobbled causeway crosses an abyss to a cliff with a blue-tiled shrine door. Low parapets on both sides carry a row of lanterns that pull the eye to the far end, where two cultists and a hellhound wait beneath a corpse hung over the doorway. The parapet is low enough to show there is nothing either side; glowing orbs float in the dark around it. The long straight approach makes the guarded door the whole view for 22 m. Seen in my own frames.
recipe: Causeway 804: 13000 x 2300 units (22 x 3.9 m), floor tile 2496 (cobbles), sky ceiling. Parapets 793 / 794: 1300 units wide strips each side, floor 5120 z (0.3 body) higher, tile 273 rock tops with brick faces; 6 lanterns tile 2493 per side, about 2000 units apart, standing on the parapet. Abyss sectors 810 / 817 either side: floor 24 bodies below the causeway, light marble 2490 walls. Entry between two 1.9-body carved pillars; far end a blue stone wall with a doorway, two kDudeCultistShotgun (202), a hellhound (type 211, tile 1270) and a hanging corpse sprite. Orb pairs (tile 624) float around the bridge.
use: The harbour: a long pier or breakwater at night with lamps on its rail, leading to the lighthouse or a moored ship with its guards at the gangway. The church: a raised path across a flooded crypt to the reliquary.
